docs.title: Car Line Tycoon Modding
docs.text:
Welcome! This site explains how to make mods for Car Line Tycoon, the tycoon game where you design cars, build the factory that makes them and sell them in your own showroom.

A Car Line Tycoon mod is a small set of JSON files. You can write them in any text editor, and the game itself can export most of them for you.

docs.title: What you can make
docs.text:
Mod type What it adds Where it shows up in the game Car model A car design: parts, colours and colour schemes Models page, Import model Livery A paint scheme with finishes Design studio, Colour schemes, Import livery Layout Walls, areas and objects of one floor Build → Sites, Import layout Scenario A Free play start with its own goals New game → Free play → Scenario Language Texts in another language Options → Language (development builds for now)

A mod can hold one type of file, or several types at once as a pack.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Read Getting started: where the Mods folder is and how the game loads it.
  2. Download an example mod, unzip it into the Mods folder and see it in the game.
  3. Open the reference page of the format you want to work with. Each page lists every field, its type, the allowed values and the limits.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Mods add content. They never replace the game's own files, so the order of your mods does not matter.
  • Mods contain data only: no 3D models, no textures and no code. Every part, colour and object comes from the game's own catalogue.
  • Every format has a JSON Schema. Point your editor at it and you get completion and error checking while you type.
  • This documentation follows the current version of the game. The changelog lists what changed for modders in each version.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: What changed for modders in each version of the game. Every file format is still at formatVersion 1.

• No changes to the file formats or to the Mods page.
  • Every new game, scenarios included, starts in April 1935.

• No changes to the file formats or to the Mods page.
  • The research tree was reorganised: showroom research moved to its own tree, and some factory-wide modules became perks. Check the completedResearch of your scenarios and the objects of your layouts against the allowed values.

• Models page: Import model lists the model files of active mods and of the exports folder and imports one as a new model. Export model writes a model to exports/.
  • Design studio: Import livery adds a livery file as a new colour scheme.
  • Build → Sites: Import layout builds a layout file on its site and floor; Export layout saves the open floor.
  • Language mods: offered in the language list of development builds, with the share of texts each one covers.
  • Mods page: a mod with a problem has a red border and shows the reason.
  • Saves: the saves list marks games played with mods, and the pause menu shows the number of active mods.
  • New Free play objective: models_10_gen3.

• First version with mods.
  • Five versioned file formats (car model, livery, layout, scenario, language) and the mod.json manifest.
  • The Mods folder, and the Mods page in the main menu with Open mod folder and Reload.
  • Scenarios from mods in New game → Free play → Scenario. The three official scenarios use the same format.
  • Saves record the active mods.

docs.title: Example mods
docs.text:
Five small mods, one for each file format. They load in the current version of the game with no warning, and every one of them is checked against the game's own readers each time this site is built.

To try one, download it, unzip it into the Mods folder and press Reload on the Mods page. Each zip holds one mod folder.

Download Type What it shows example_model.zip Car model A small open car with every part and colour, exported from the game. Import it from the Models page. example_livery.zip Livery A two-tone blue livery with metallic and chrome finishes and an anchor emblem. Import it in the studio's Colour schemes. example_layout.zip Layout A walled production hall with a splitter and a belt for the factory's ground floor. Import it from Build → Sites on an empty part of the site. example_scenario.zip Scenario «Corner Garage»: one line, a showroom, two goals. Pick it in New game → Free play → Scenario. example_language.zip Language Three texts of the Mods page in a new language entry. Pick it in Options → Language (development builds). all-examples.zip All five The five folders above in one zip.

docs.title: Inside an example
docs.text:
example_livery/
  mod.json
  harbour_blue.clt-livery.json

mod.json:

{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.mod",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": ">=0.6.1",
  "id": "example_livery",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "name": { "en": "Example livery: Harbour Blue" },
  "description": { "en": "A two-tone blue livery with a chrome trim, to import in the studio's colour schemes." },
  "authors": ["Car Line Tycoon modding docs"],
  "type": "livery"
}

docs.title: Make your own from an example
docs.text:
1. Copy the example folder and give it a new name, such as my_livery.
  2. In mod.json, set id to the same name, then change name, description, authors and version.
  3. Rename the content file and change its id.
  4. Edit the fields. The reference page of each format lists what you can change.
  5. Press Reload on the Mods page. If the row turns red, the troubleshooting page explains the warning.

docs.title: The Mods folder
docs.text:
The game reads mods from one folder on your computer, next to your saves.

The quickest way to open it: start the game, choose Mods in the main menu, then press Open mod folder. The game creates the folder if it does not exist yet and opens it in your file browser.

You can also find it yourself:

System Mods folder Windows %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\DefaultCompany\Car Line Tycoon\Mods macOS ~/Library/Application Support/DefaultCompany/Car Line Tycoon/Mods Linux ~/.config/unity3d/DefaultCompany/Car Line Tycoon/Mods

docs.title: What a mod looks like
docs.text:
The game accepts three shapes of mod inside the Mods folder.

A mod folder with a manifest. This is the recommended shape. The folder name is the mod's id, and mod.json describes the mod (see Manifest):

Mods/
  harbour_cars/
    mod.json
    models/
      harbour_coupe.clt-model.json
      harbour_van.clt-model.json

A folder without a manifest. The game reads every mod file inside it as a pack named after the folder. The folder name must be a valid id.

A single file. A file such as harbour_blue.clt-livery.json placed straight in Mods/ is a mod of its own. Its id is the part of the file name before .clt-.

A few rules apply to every shape:

  • Ids use lower-case letters, digits and underscores, start with a letter and are 3 to 41 characters long.
  • The game finds mod files up to three folder levels below the mod folder. You can organise them in subfolders such as models/ or layouts/.
  • The file extension tells the game what a file is: .clt-model.json, .clt-livery.json, .clt-layout.json, .clt-scenario.json or .clt-lang.json. Other files are left alone.
  • Symbolic links and junctions are skipped.
  • The exports folder belongs to the game: files you export from the game go there. Its files show up in the import lists, and the Mods page leaves it out.

docs.title: The Mods page
docs.text:
Choose Mods in the main menu. Every mod has a row with:

  • a switch to turn it on or off,
  • its name (in your language when the manifest has it),
  • its version, its authors and its type,
  • a red border and a red warning line when something is wrong (see Troubleshooting).

The game reads the Mods folder each time the main menu opens. After you change a file, press Reload to read it again. Mods are listed in alphabetical order of their English name.

A new mod starts switched on. The game keeps your choices in mods.json, next to the Mods folder.

docs.title: How the game uses mods
docs.text:
A mod is active when it is switched on and has no warning. Active mods show up in the game's own pages:

Type In the game Car model Models page: Import model lists the model files; pick one to see the same preview as a pasted design, then import it as a new model. Export model in a model's details writes exports/<name>.clt-model.json. Livery Design studio, Colour schemes: Import livery adds the file as a new colour scheme. It needs the colour schemes research. Layout Build → Sites: Import layout builds the file's walls, areas and objects; Export layout saves the open floor of the open site. Scenario New game → Free play: the Scenario selector lists the scenarios of active mods after the official ones, with the mod's name. Language Options → Language and the language list of the main menu, with the share of texts the language covers. Development builds only for now.

When you start or load a game, the game writes the active mods into the save: id, version, type and a hash of their files. The saves list marks such saves with mods, and the pause menu shows Active mods: N. A save that used a mod you later removed still loads.

docs.title: Achievements
docs.text:
Car models, liveries, layouts and languages do not affect achievements.

A scenario from a mod follows the rule every Free play start follows: the game counts as assisted, and earns no achievements, when it starts on Easy, with a fixed amount of $100,000 or more, or with more than one ready assembly line.

docs.title: Versions and compatibility
docs.text:
Every mod file starts with three fields:

  • format: the kind of file, for example car-line-tycoon.livery.
  • formatVersion: the version of that format. Every format is at version 1 today.
  • gameVersion: the game version that wrote the file. The game ignores it in content files.

The game reads files of its own format version and older ones. A file with a newer formatVersion gets the warning Requires a newer game version.

In mod.json, gameVersion has its own meaning: the oldest game version the mod needs, written as "0.6.1" or ">=0.6.1". When the game is older, the mod gets the same warning and the game does not use it.

Fields the game does not know are ignored. You can add your own notes to a file as extra fields, and a file written for a later version still loads when it only adds fields.

Game version What it reads 0.6.0 The five formats and mod.json, the Mods page, scenarios from mods 0.6.1 and later Import and export of models, liveries and layouts; language mods in development builds

The changelog has the details.

docs.title: Planned
docs.text: These are ideas we are working on for the modding side of Car Line Tycoon. Plans can change, so this page has no dates. The changelog records what has actually arrived.

docs.title: Steam Workshop
docs.text: We would like players to share models, liveries, layouts and scenarios on the Steam Workshop and subscribe to them from there. The plan is to keep the same file formats, so the mods you write today should move to the Workshop as they are. A save would also remember which Workshop items it used.

docs.title: Lua scripting
docs.text: We are studying Lua scripts for mods during Early Access. A script would react to events of the game, such as a new day, a sale or a finished research topic, and use a limited set of game functions. Scripts would run in a sandbox, with no access to your files or to the network.

docs.title: More languages
docs.text: The game is getting more official languages. Language mods will also be offered in release builds once the game can load the fonts they bring.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: When something is wrong with a mod, its row on the Mods page gets a red border and one red warning line. The game does not use the mod until the problem is fixed, whatever the position of its switch. The game shows one warning per mod, for the first problem it finds; after a fix, press Reload to see whether another one follows.

docs.title: Invalid file: file name
docs.text:
The game could not read the file, or the file is incomplete. Check, in this order:

  1. Is it valid JSON? A missing comma, an extra comma before } or ], or a missing quote is enough. A JSON validator or an editor with the JSON Schemas points to the line.
  2. Is the header right? format must match the file type exactly (car-line-tycoon.livery for a .clt-livery.json file), and formatVersion must be 1.
  3. Are the types right? Numbers are plain numbers (4), texts are in quotes ("Harbour Blue"), true and false have no quotes, and lists are in square brackets. A word where a number belongs makes the file invalid.
  4. Are the required fields there? Each reference page marks them. The most common misses: id, an empty parts list in a model, objects/walls/areas in a layout (write [] when they are empty), texts in a scenario.
  5. Are the values allowed? An id with capital letters or spaces, an emblem colour outside the palette, an area kind the game does not have, a scenario objective that is not a Free play objective. The allowed values page lists them.

When the warning names mod.json, the problem is in the manifest. See Manifest.

docs.title: Requires a newer game version
docs.text: Either the mod's mod.json asks for a newer game in gameVersion, or one of its files has a formatVersion above 1. Update the game, or lower the version in the mod if it was set by mistake.

docs.title: File too large: file name
docs.text: A mod file can be up to 2 MB, and a language file up to 8 MB. Split a large mod into several files, for example one model per file.

docs.title: mod.json is missing or invalid
docs.text: A folder in the Mods folder has no mod.json, and its name is not a valid id, so the game cannot use it as a pack. Add a mod.json, or rename the folder with lower-case letters, digits and underscores (3 to 41 characters, starting with a letter).

docs.title: Folder name does not match the ID in mod.json
docs.text: The folder's name and the id in its mod.json must be the same text. Rename one of them.

docs.title: The mod contains no usable files
docs.text:
The game found no file it can use in the mod. Check that:

  • the files end in .clt-model.json, .clt-livery.json, .clt-layout.json, .clt-scenario.json or .clt-lang.json,
  • the file types match the manifest's type (a livery mod reads only livery files; use pack for several types),
  • the files are at most three folder levels below the mod folder.

docs.title: Messages during import
docs.text:
Message Where What to do No files of this type in the mod folder. An import list No active mod has a file of this type. Check that the mod is switched on and has no warning, then press Reload on the Mods page. This livery contains unsupported colours. Studio, Import livery A colour uses an unknown channel, a channel twice, a value that is not #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA, or a finish on a channel that takes none. See Livery. Layout imported: N placed, M skipped Build → Sites Skipped pieces were refused by the building rules: the cell is taken, the money ran out, the object needs research, or the site is not yours yet. See Layout. Could not save to path Any export The game could not write in the exports folder. Check that the disk has space and the folder is writable.

When an imported model shows a problem in its preview, the same message appears as for a pasted design: a part the catalogue does not have, parts that do not fit together, or colours the game does not accept. See Car model.

docs.title: My mod does not show up at all
docs.text:
• The file or folder must sit directly in the Mods folder: Mods/my_mod/mod.json or Mods/my_file.clt-livery.json. A mod one folder deeper, such as Mods/downloads/my_mod/, is read as a mod called downloads.
  • The game reads the folder when the main menu opens. Press Reload after a change.
  • Folders and files that are symbolic links or junctions are skipped. Copy the real files into the Mods folder.
  • Make sure you are looking in the right folder: Open mod folder on the Mods page opens it.

docs.title: My scenario is not in the list
docs.text:
A scenario shows up in New game → Free play → Scenario when its mod is switched on and has no warning. Scenarios of mods come after the three official ones.

When the game refuses to start a scenario, check startChapter: it must be empty or one of the story chapters.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text:
Car Line Tycoon reads six kinds of JSON file. Five carry content, and the manifest describes a mod folder.

File Extension or name Format id Reference Schema Manifest mod.json car-line-tycoon.mod Manifest manifest.schema.json Car model .clt-model.json car-line-tycoon.model Car model model.schema.json Livery .clt-livery.json car-line-tycoon.livery Livery livery.schema.json Layout .clt-layout.json car-line-tycoon.layout Layout layout.schema.json Scenario .clt-scenario.json car-line-tycoon.scenario Scenario scenario.schema.json Language .clt-lang.json car-line-tycoon.language Language language.schema.json

docs.title: The header
docs.text:
Every file starts with the same three fields:

Field Type Value format string The format id from the table above. A file with another value is refused. formatVersion integer 1. A higher number is refused with Requires a newer game version. gameVersion string The game version that wrote the file, for example "0.6.2". Content files: informative only. Manifest: the oldest game version the mod needs.

docs.title: Rules for every file
docs.text:
• Encoding. Save files as UTF-8. A byte order mark at the start is fine.
  • Size. A file can be up to 2 MB. A language file can be up to 8 MB. A larger file gets the warning File too large.
  • Types. Write numbers as plain JSON numbers (4) and texts as JSON strings ("Harbour Blue"). A value of the wrong kind, such as a word where a number belongs, makes the file invalid.
  • Unknown fields. The game ignores fields it does not know, at the top level and inside lists.
  • Ids. An id uses lower-case letters a–z, digits and underscores, starts with a letter and is 3 to 41 characters long: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$.
  • Data only. No format carries a mesh, a texture or a script. Parts, colours, emblems and objects are chosen among the game's own; the allowed values page lists them.

docs.title: When the game checks a file
docs.text:
The game checks a file twice.

  1. When it reads the Mods folder. The game reads every file with its format reader. A file that is not JSON, has the wrong header, is too large or misses a required field gives the mod a warning, and the game does not use the mod. For a scenario the game also checks the objectives and the texts at this point.
  2. When you use the file in the game. Importing a model, a livery or a layout runs the game's own rules: parts must exist, colours must use the game's channels, objects must fit where they are placed. The reference page of each format says what the game checks at this step.

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
Each format has a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), generated from the game's code. A schema checks the structure of a file and the allowed ids, so your editor can flag a typo before you start the game.

Format Schema URL Manifest https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/manifest.schema.json Car model https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/model.schema.json Livery https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/livery.schema.json Layout https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/layout.schema.json Scenario https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/scenario.schema.json Language https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/language.schema.json

In Visual Studio Code, add this to your settings to check every mod file as you type:

{
  "json.schemas": [
    { "fileMatch": ["mod.json"], "url": "https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/manifest.schema.json" },
    { "fileMatch": ["*.clt-model.json"], "url": "https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/model.schema.json" },
    { "fileMatch": ["*.clt-livery.json"], "url": "https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/livery.schema.json" },
    { "fileMatch": ["*.clt-layout.json"], "url": "https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/layout.schema.json" },
    { "fileMatch": ["*.clt-scenario.json"], "url": "https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/scenario.schema.json" },
    { "fileMatch": ["*.clt-lang.json"], "url": "https://carlinetycoon.github.io/schemas/language.schema.json" }
  ]
}

A few rules are outside what a schema can say, such as the file size and the checks the game makes when you import a file. The reference pages list them.

docs.title: Language (.clt-lang.json)
docs.text:
A language file holds the game's texts in another language, one entry per text key. A key the file leaves out shows the English text, so a translation can grow a little at a time.

Schema: language.schema.json · Example: example_language.zip

Development builds only for now

Every build of the game reads and checks language files, and the Mods page lists them. The language list in Options offers them in development builds of the game. Release builds do not list language mods yet.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.language",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": "0.6.0",
  "code": "en-GB",
  "name": "English (example)",
  "entries": [
    { "key": "front.mods", "value": "Mods and add-ons" },
    { "key": "mods.reload", "value": "Read the mod folder again" },
    { "key": "mods.open_folder", "value": "Show the mod folder" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description format string yes Always car-line-tycoon.language. formatVersion integer yes 1. gameVersion string no The game version that wrote the file. Informative. code string yes The language tag, such as pt-BR or uk: 2 to 12 letters, digits and hyphens. name string yes The language's own name, as the language list shows it: Português, Українська. font string no A TTF or OTF font file inside the mod folder, as a relative path such as fonts/MyFont.ttf. fontLicense string with font The font's licence, for example SIL Open Font License 1.1. Required when font is set. entries array of entries yes The texts, up to 20,000.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Field Type Required Description key string yes A key of the game's English text table, such as front.mods. Each key at most once in a file. value string yes The text in this language. Not empty.

docs.title: Keys and placeholders
docs.text:
The game looks keys up without regard to letter case. Keys the game does not have are ignored.

Some texts contain placeholders in braces, such as {file}, {count} or {path}. Keep every placeholder exactly as it is in English: the game replaces it with a value when it shows the text. A line break inside a text is written \n.

docs.title: In the game
docs.text:
• A language mod that is active joins the language list in Options → Language and on the main menu, with its name and the share of the game's texts it covers, for example Português · 62%.
  • When the player picks it, the game shows the file's text for every key it has and the English text for the others.
  • When code is a language the game already lists, the mod fills that language. Any other code becomes a new entry in the list.

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text: The game checks the font and fontLicense fields: the path must stay inside the mod folder (no drive letter, no ..), and a font needs a licence. The game does not load the font file yet, so letters missing from the game's own font show as empty boxes.

docs.title: What the game checks
docs.text:
• the header,
  • code is 2 to 12 letters, digits or hyphens, and name is not empty,
  • entries has at most 20,000 entries, each with a key and a value, and no key twice,
  • font, when set, is a relative path inside the mod folder and comes with a fontLicense.

A language file can be up to 8 MB.

docs.title: Layout (.clt-layout.json)
docs.text:
A layout holds the walls, areas and objects of one floor of one site. Importing it builds every piece at its normal price, following the same rules as building by hand.

Schema: layout.schema.json · Example: example_layout.zip

docs.title: The easy way: export from the game
docs.text: Open Build → Sites, pick the site and the floor, and press Export layout. The game writes the file in the exports folder of the Mods folder, named after the site and the floor: industrial_1.clt-layout.json for the factory's ground floor.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.layout",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": "0.6.0",
  "id": "small_hall",
  "name": "Small hall",
  "site": "industrial",
  "floor": 0,
  "objects": [
    { "definition": "split", "x": 25, "z": 14, "rotation": "North" },
    { "definition": "belt", "x": 20, "z": 7, "rotation": "East" }
  ],
  "walls": [
    { "x1": 18, "z1": 5, "x2": 42, "z2": 5 },
    { "x1": 42, "z1": 5, "x2": 42, "z2": 35 },
    { "x1": 42, "z1": 35, "x2": 18, "z2": 35 },
    { "x1": 18, "z1": 35, "x2": 18, "z2": 5 }
  ],
  "areas": [
    { "kind": "Production", "x": 18, "z": 5, "width": 24, "depth": 30 }
  ]
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description format string yes Always car-line-tycoon.layout. formatVersion integer yes 1. gameVersion string no The game version that wrote the file. Informative. id string yes The file's id. Pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$. name string no The layout's name. site string yes industrial (the factory) or urban (the showroom). floor integer no The floor, 0 for the ground floor. The factory has floor 0 only; the showroom has floors 0 to 5. Default 0. objects array of objects yes Up to 5000. Can be empty. walls array of walls yes Up to 5000. Can be empty. areas array of areas yes Up to 5000. Can be empty.

Positions are cells of the site's building grid; one cell is 2 metres. Export a layout from the game to see the coordinates of your own buildings.

docs.title: Object
docs.text: Field Type Required Description definition string yes The object's id, such as belt or split. See objects. x integer yes The object's cell on the x axis. z integer yes The object's cell on the z axis. fineX integer no For free-standing furniture: the offset inside the cell, in sixteenths of a cell, 0 to 15. fineZ integer no Same, on the z axis. rotation string yes North, East, South or West, in any letter case.

docs.title: Wall
docs.text:
A straight wall from one grid point to another.

Field Type Required Description x1, z1 integer yes The start point. x2, z2 integer yes The end point.

docs.title: Area
docs.text: Field Type Required Description kind string yes Production, Warehouse, Services, Yard, Commercial or Workshop, in any letter case. x, z integer yes The first cell of the area. width integer yes The width in cells, 1 or more. depth integer yes The depth in cells, 1 or more.

docs.title: How the import builds a layout
docs.text:
The game builds the pieces in this order, on the site and floor written in the file:

  1. The building. When the walls run around a closed rectangle, the game builds that rectangle as one building, with the same tool as the Wall rectangle in the build menu. The walls on its four sides count as placed or skipped together.
  2. The inner walls. Every other wall is built as a single wall. A single wall can only stand inside a building.
  3. The areas.
  4. The objects.

Every piece costs its normal price and goes through the normal building rules. When the game refuses a piece (the cell is taken, the money runs out, the object is unknown or needs research, the site is not yours yet), it skips that piece and carries on. At the end the game shows Layout imported: N placed, M skipped.

Keep one building per layout file. When the walls of a file do not close one rectangle around all of them, the game builds them as single walls, and walls outside an existing building are skipped.

docs.title: What the layout leaves out
docs.text: A layout holds construction only. Staff, car models, stock, research and money stay as they are in the player's game.

docs.title: What the game checks when it reads the file
docs.text:
• the header and the id,
  • site is present and floor is 0 or more,
  • objects, walls and areas are present, with at most 5000 entries each,
  • every object has a definition and a known rotation, and fineX/fineZ are between 0 and 15,
  • every area has a known kind and a positive width and depth.

The rest is checked piece by piece during the import.

docs.title: Livery (.clt-livery.json)
docs.text:
A livery is a paint scheme: a colour and a paint finish for each colour channel of a car, plus an emblem. In the design studio, Import livery adds it to the open model as a new colour scheme.

Schema: livery.schema.json · Example: example_livery.zip

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.livery",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": "0.6.0",
  "id": "harbour_blue",
  "name": "Harbour Blue",
  "colors": [
    { "channel": "body", "value": "#2F5D8A", "finish": "metallic" },
    { "channel": "roof", "value": "#E8E1CF" },

Informative. id string yes The file's id. Pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$. name string no The colour scheme's name in the studio. When it is empty, the studio uses the file name. colors array of colours yes At least one colour, at most one per channel. emblem emblem yes A complete emblem.

docs.title: Colour
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description channel string yes body, roof, interior, trim, chassis, wheels or powertrain. value string yes #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA, hexadecimal. finish string no normal, metallic, matte, pearl, flake or chrome, in any letter case. Leave it out for normal paint.

Only body, roof, trim and wheels take a finish other than normal. Channels you leave out get the studio's default colours when you import the livery.

docs.title: Emblem
docs.text:
All seven fields are required, and each takes one of the game's own values. The allowed values page lists them.

Field Type Description shape string The badge's shape, such as shield or circle. pattern string The badge's pattern, such as plain or horizontal. color1 string The first badge colour, from the emblem palette (navy, cream, ...). color2 string The second badge colour, from the emblem palette. icon string The badge's icon, such as star or anchor. iconColor string The icon's colour, from the emblem palette. mascotFinish string The bonnet mascot's finish: chrome or brass.

Note

The studio imports a livery's colours. The emblem must be valid for the file to load, and the company keeps its own emblem.

docs.title: What the game checks
docs.text:
When it reads the Mods folder, the game checks the header, the id, that every colour has a channel, a value and a known finish, and that the emblem uses the game's values.

When you import the livery in the studio:

  • every channel must be one of the seven above, and each channel at most once,
  • every value must be #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA,
  • a finish other than normal must be on body, roof, trim or wheels.

A livery that fails these checks shows This livery contains unsupported colours.

Import livery needs the colour schemes research, like Duplicate this scheme in the studio.

docs.title: Manifest (mod.json)
docs.text:
mod.json sits at the top of a mod folder and tells the game what the mod is. The folder name must be the same as the mod's id.

Schema: manifest.schema.json

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.mod",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": ">=0.6.1",
  "id": "harbour_cars",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "name": { "en": "Harbour Cars", "it": "Auto del porto" },
  "description": { "en": "Two small cars and a blue livery." },
  "authors": ["Aria", "Tom"],
  "type": "pack"
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description format string yes Always car-line-tycoon.mod. formatVersion integer yes 1. gameVersion string no The oldest game version the mod needs: "0.6.1" or ">=0.6.1". The game compares it with its own version. Leave it out, or write a value the game cannot read, and the game does not check it. id string yes The mod's id. It must match the folder name. Pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$. version string yes Your version of the mod, shown on the Mods page as v1.2.0. Any non-empty text. name object yes The mod's name per language: keys are two-letter codes such as "en", "it", "fr", "es", "de", values are texts. At least one entry. description object no The mod's description per language, in the same shape as name. authors array of strings no The authors. The Mods page joins them with commas. type string yes model, livery, layout, scenario, language or pack.

docs.title: How the type works
docs.text:
• A mod of type model, livery, layout, scenario or language reads only the files of that type. Files of other types inside it are left alone.
  • A mod of type pack reads all five types.
  • A mod needs at least one file it can use. A mod folder with no usable file gets the warning The mod contains no usable files.

docs.title: Names and languages
docs.text: The Mods page shows the name in the player's language when name has it, then the English one, then the first one in the file. description works the same way. Use two-letter language codes: en, it, fr, es, de, ru, zh and so on.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• The folder name and id must be the same, otherwise the mod gets the warning Folder name does not match the ID in mod.json.
  • When a manifest cannot be read, or misses id, version, name or a valid type, the mod gets the warning Invalid file: mod.json.
  • A folder without mod.json works too: the game reads it as a pack named after the folder. Its folder name must then be a valid id, otherwise the warning is mod.json is missing or invalid.
  • When two mods have the same id, the game keeps the first one it finds.

docs.title: Car model (.clt-model.json)
docs.text:
A car model file holds a design from the studio: its parts, its colours, its colour schemes and its option packages. The game works out everything else (price, performance, production time) from its own catalogue when you import the file, so a model file can never carry numbers of its own.

Schema: model.schema.json · Example: example_model.zip

docs.title: The easy way: export from the game
docs.text: Open the Models page, select a model and press Export model in its details. The game writes exports/<model_name>.clt-model.json in the Mods folder (the model's name in lower case, with underscores) and shows the path. Copy that file into your mod folder and edit it from there.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A shortened file (an exported file lists every part and all seven colour channels):

{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.model",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": "0.6.2",
  "id": "harbour_coupe",
  "name": "Harbour Coupe",
  "parts": [
    { "category": "body", "part": "Body_Taxi" },
    { "category": "bonnet", "part": "Bonnet_Taxi" },
    { "category": "chassis", "part": "Chassis_T_Wider" },
    { "category": "wheels", "part": "Wheel_Taxi_Stamp" },
    { "category": "motor", "part": "Motor_Bucket" }
  ],
  "colors": [
    { "channel": "body", "value": "#2F5D8A", "finish": 1 },
    { "channel": "trim", "value": "#C4C6C7" }
  ],
  "schemes": [
    {
      "id": "default",
      "name": "",
      "colors": [
        { "channel": "body", "value": "#2F5D8A", "finish": 1 },
        { "channel": "trim", "value": "#C4C6C7" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description format string yes Always car-line-tycoon.model. formatVersion integer yes 1. gameVersion string no The game version that wrote the file. Informative. id string yes The file's id. Pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$. name string no The model's name. The import uses it as the new model's name. parts array of parts yes The car's parts, one per category. At least one. colors array of colours no The model's default colours, at most one per channel. schemes array of schemes no The model's colour schemes. packages array of packages no Option packages (engine, armour, armament).

docs.title: Part
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description category string yes The part's category, such as body, wheels or motor. See part categories. part string yes The part's id in the game's catalogue.

The catalogue has several hundred parts, and the studio knows which of them fit together. Build the car in the studio, export it, and copy the ids from the exported file.

docs.title: Colour
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description channel string yes body, roof, interior, trim, chassis, wheels or powertrain. value string yes #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA, hexadecimal. finish integer no The paint finish as a number: 0 normal, 1 metallic, 2 matte, 3 pearl, 4 flake, 5 chrome. Leave it out for normal paint.

Only body, roof, trim and wheels take a finish other than normal. A finish other than normal also needs its paint research in the player's company.

Note

A model file stores the finish as a number. A livery file stores it as a name. Both come from the same list of paint finishes.

docs.title: Scheme
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description id string no The scheme's id inside the model. The first scheme of an exported file is default and repeats the default colours. name string no The scheme's name. colors array of colours yes The scheme's colours.

More than one scheme needs the colour schemes research in the player's company.

docs.title: Package
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string yes The package's id. version integer yes The package's version, 1 or more. kind integer yes 0 engine, 1 armour, 2 armament. parts array of parts yes The parts the package adds or swaps. removals array of strings no The part categories the package removes.

docs.title: What the game checks
docs.text:
When it reads the Mods folder, the game checks the header, the id and that parts has at least one entry.

When you pick the file in Import model, the Models page shows the same preview as a pasted design and checks everything else:

  • every part exists in the catalogue and fits the parts around it,
  • every colour uses a known channel and a valid value,
  • every package fits the car.

The preview also lists any part your company has not unlocked yet (it needs research or a later era). A file that fails these checks shows the same message as a pasted design that fails them.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The file name is up to you. The import lists files by their name without the extension.
  • To share several models, put them in one model mod, for example in a models/ subfolder.
  • Copy as text and Paste a design on the Models page use a related text format, car-line-tycoon.design. Use model files for mods: they have an id and the shared header.

docs.title: Scenario (.clt-scenario.json)
docs.text:
A scenario is a Free play start with its own goals. It sets the starting money, the ready factory and showroom, the objectives, and optionally a story chapter, research already done and one special rule. The game's three official scenarios are written in this same format and read by the same reader.

Schema: scenario.schema.json · Example: example_scenario.zip

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "format": "car-line-tycoon.scenario",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "gameVersion": "0.6.0",
  "id": "corner_garage",
  "startingFundsCents": 0,
  "readyLines": 1,
  "readyShowroom": true,
  "objectives": ["sales_100", "reputation_60"],
  "startChapter": "",
  "completedResearch": [],
  "rule": "",
  "texts": [
    {
      "lang": "en",
      "title": "Corner Garage",
      "description": "One assembly line and a small showroom. Sell a hundred cars and earn a good name in town."
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description format string yes Always car-line-tycoon.scenario. formatVersion integer yes 1. gameVersion string no The game version that wrote the file. Informative. id string yes The scenario's id. Pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$. In the game it becomes <mod id>.<scenario id>, for example example_scenario.corner_garage. startingFundsCents integer no The starting money in cents: 4000000 is $40,000. 0 gives the standard Free play money for the chosen difficulty. Default 0. readyLines integer yes Assembly lines in the ready factory, 1 to 4. readyShowroom boolean no true to start with a ready showroom. Default false. objectives array of strings yes The goals, 1 to 40, from the game's Free play objectives. startChapter string no A story chapter published on day one, such as tensions, or "" for none. See story chapters. completedResearch array of strings no Research topics done from the start, up to 40. The game adds the topics each of them needs. See research topics. rule string no daily_fleet_orders or "" for none. texts array of texts yes The title and description per language. At least one.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description lang string yes A two-letter language code: en, it, fr, es, de, ... title string yes The scenario's title in the Scenario selector. description string no The description in the scenario's tooltip, above the mod's name and the goals.

The game shows the text of the player's language, then the English one, then the first one in the file.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
A scenario can add one rule the game knows:

Rule What it does daily_fleet_orders A fleet order of six cars arrives every day the order slot is free. The official scenario Fleets uses it.

docs.title: How the scenario starts a game
docs.text:
1. The player picks the scenario in New game → Free play → Scenario. The scenario sets the start: the ready factory with readyLines lines, the showroom when readyShowroom is true, and the money. The player still picks the difficulty.
  2. When the game starts, the research topics in completedResearch are done, with every topic they need first. Ids the game does not know are ignored.
  3. When startChapter is set, the game publishes that chapter, and the chapters before it, on day one.
  4. The goals of the game are the scenario's objectives.

The scenario's id is kept in the save. When the mod is later removed, the save still loads and plays on.

docs.title: Achievements
docs.text: A scenario from a mod follows the rule of every Free play start. The game counts as assisted, and earns no achievements, when it starts on Easy, with startingFundsCents of 10000000 ($100,000) or more, or with readyLines above 1.

docs.title: What the game checks
docs.text:
When it reads the Mods folder:

  • the header and the id,
  • startingFundsCents is 0 or more and readyLines is between 1 and 4,
  • rule is empty or daily_fleet_orders,
  • objectives has 1 to 40 entries, none empty, and every one is a Free play objective of the game,
  • completedResearch has at most 40 entries, none empty,
  • texts has at least one entry, each with a lang and a title.

When the game starts: an unknown startChapter stops the game from starting. Use one of the story chapters or leave it empty.
